Linear regression is a statistical method used to model the relationship between a dependent variable and one or more independent variables. It helps us understand how the typical value of the dependent variable changes when any one of the independent variables is varied, while the other independent variables are held fixed.

In simpler terms, imagine you have a set of data points that represent the relationship between two things, like the height of a plant and the amount of water it receives. Linear regression can help you find a line that best fits these data points, so you can predict the height of the plant based on the amount of water it receives.

The line is called a "regression line" because it helps us "regress" or predict the value of the dependent variable based on the independent variable(s). The slope of the line tells us how much the dependent variable changes for a one-unit increase in the independent variable(s). The intercept of the line tells us the value of the dependent variable when the independent variable(s) are zero.

A web crawler, also known as a web spider or web robot, is a program that automatically visits and indexes the pages of a website or the entire internet. The primary purpose of a web crawler is to gather information about the web, such as the content of the pages, the links on the pages, and the structure of the website.
Web crawlers work by following links from one page to another, starting from a set of initial pages called "seed" pages. They then visit each page they encounter and follow any links that point to other pages. This process is repeated until the crawler has visited a large number of pages and has collected a comprehensive index of the web.
Web crawlers are used by search engines to index the web and provide search results to users. They are also used by websites to gather information about their own content and to improve their search engine optimization (SEO) efforts. Web crawlers can be programmed to follow specific rules and parameters, such as only visiting certain types of pages

1. Double 34: \( 34 \times 2 = 68 \)
2. Double the result: \( 68 \times 2 = 136 \)

It helps us understand how the typical value of the dependent variable changes when any one of the independent variables is varied, while the other independent variables are held fixed.

In simpler terms, imagine you have a bunch of data points that show how much something changes as you change another thing. Linear regression helps you find a straight line that best fits these data points. This line shows you how much one thing changes for every unit change in the other thing. 

For example, if you're trying to predict how much a car will cost based on its age, you might use linear regression to find a line that shows how much the cost increases for each year the car has been in use. 

The "line" in linear regression is called a "regression line" or "line of best fit." It's the line that minimizes the distance between the line and all the data points.

In a blockchain-based network, each transaction is recorded in a block, which is then added to a chain of blocks, creating a permanent and immutable record of all transactions. This makes it difficult for anyone to alter or delete a transaction, as any attempt to do so would require changing the entire chain of blocks, which is computationally expensive and time-consuming.
